commentary.commText: Yuvraj Singh rings the Lord's bell. The players and the match officials line up to observe a minute's silence for the passing of Sir Garfield Sobers. West Indies greats - Brian Lara and Clive Lloyd are in the house. Right then, it's action time now. In Bumrah's absence, Arshdeep Singh has the new ball in his hand. He'll start from the Pavilion End with two slips in place. Here we go..

- 400th International game featuring both Virat Kohli & Rohit Sharma together

India’s toss record in ODIs since Dec 2023 
Mat 29 | Tosses won 4 | Tosses lost 25

- Lord’s has hosted five ODIs post the 2019 World Cup final – each of the five won by the side batting first with win margins of 52 runs, 100 runs, 100 runs, 186 runs, and five runs.
Jofra Archer [in a chat with Sky Cricket]

Here's the update from BCCI - "Jasprit Bumrah had an impact injury on his left knee while fielding in the second ODI in Cardiff. He was not available for selection for the third ODI due to reactive swelling in his left knee."
India (Playing XI): Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill(c), Virat Kohli, Ishan Kishan(w), Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, Axar Patel, Gurnoor Brar, Prince Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna
England (Playing XI): Ben Duckett, Jacob Bethell, Joe Root, Harry Brook(c), Jos Buttler(w), Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Gus Atkinson, Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid, Josh Tongue

Shubman Gill: [On losing the toss] We were bowling first. We have got three changes. Boom misses out, he's unavailable due to some knee injury. And so is Washington Sundar. Dube also misses out. KL comes in, Prince Yadav comes in, and Arshdeep comes back into the team. [On selecting Arshdeep Singh] We're not the one who relies on stats so much. We think he's a great bowler, and we were looking for four seamers on this ground. We have seen in the middle overs, spinners don't really offer much as compared to the fast bowlers. [On what India need to improve from the second ODI] I think we were in a great position up until the 25 overs of the match, and then we lost too many wickets in the middle overs, end of the middle overs. So hopefully, if you're in that kind of position, we post a good total close to 280-300. And then we have seen it's not easy to score freely in the past couple of matches. So hopefully, if we are able to get good runs and put the team in a comfortable position.

Harry Brook: We're going to have a bat today. It looks like a good surface, hopefully we can get a decent score on the board and put them under pressure. Tongue comes back in for Saqib. [On the most pleasing aspect of England's win in Cardiff] Well, there's loads of periods, I thought we did really well through the middle overs with the ball to restrict them. I can't remember what the figures were, but I think they went for 30 runs in 10 overs or so. And then the way that Rooty batted sets a great template for all of our batters. [On the chance to seal the series] Yeah, it'd be beautiful, wouldn't it? Hopefully we'll be lifting that trophy at the end of the day, but we've got to go in there, assess conditions as well as we can, and adapt to the conditions as well.
England have won the toss and have opted to bat

The hosts strengthened their pace attack for the second ODI and emerged victorious. They are unlikely to make any drastic changes. India will be forced to make a change as Washington has been ruled out with a hamstring injury. It'll be interesting to see who replaces him. A spinning all-rounder in Harsh Dubey or a frontline spinner in Kuldeep Yadav? If KL Rahul is fit, he should slot back into the XI. Promises to be a cracking game of cricket. Stick around for toss and team updates..

England also have a few issues to address in the batting department. While the openers survived umpteen plays and misses at Edgbaston and forged a fifty partnership, both left-handers were dismissed cheaply in Cardiff. Captain Brook hasn't translated his T20I form into the ODIs. Jos Buttler's highest score this year in ODIs is 38. Joe Root, meanwhile, is amassing runs for fun. His scores this year - 61, 75, 111*, 76* and 99* - are a testament to it. England enjoy good batting depth. Dawson recorded his maiden fifty batting at number eight in Edgbaston while the likes of Curran, Jacks and Atkinson chipped in with handy runs to support Root.

For India, Gill has been in sublime touch but both his knocks this series came to premature ends - walked off retired hurt on 80 in the 1st ODI and a sharp catch led to his downfall in the 2nd ODI. Rohit's ODI career has been the talk of the town. He's had two below-par outings this series and has crossed 50 only once in eight innings this year. With many rumours flying around, the BCCI issued this clarification - I0$ Kohli, after a rare failure in Birmingham, notched up his trademark fifty before Jofra dismissed him for the second time in as many outings. Shreyas Iyer, who was India's best batter in the T20Is, threw his wicket away in the first ODI but his fifty ensured India crossed 200 on Thursday. Unlike the first ODI, the all-rounders contributed nothing as Washi, Axar and Dube scored 3 runs in total.

10:00 Local Time, 09:00 GMT, 14:30 IST: Lord's has hosted five ODIs since the iconic 2019 World Cup Final. Teams batting first have won all five matches with the margin of victory exceeding 100 runs on three occasions. In this series, however, the chasing team has won both matches, although not convincingly. India hunted down 259 at Edgbaston on the back of fifties from Gill, Axar and Washington. England levelled the series in Cardiff by chasing down India's 233, thanks to Root's unbeaten 99. Since the 2023 WC, England have won just two of the eight bilateral ODI series. India, in the same period, have won four and lost three. What's in store today? Hello everyone and a warm welcome to the series-decider.
